tutorials.name: shiksha-teacher-roster-tutorial

tutorials.note: The embedded teacher dashboard shows a fictional course and roster. Learner progress and artifact data are controlled local fixtures, not real participant records or measured outcomes.

03  Select a learner and expand a concept. In progress is not a mastery claim.

06  Close the preview to return to the same learner and their course work.

tutorials.name: shiksha-learner-memory-tutorial
tutorials.title: See how learner memory changes
tutorials.note: Demonstrates the project's custom learner-memory structure in the actual Graph Memory panel, not the separate hosted Memory Store. Two prior diagnostic records and the before/pending/after snapshots are synthetic fixtures. The new evidence quote comes from the answer typed in this recording. No live memory worker, model or state reducer was run, and no real course was activated. A correct response improves the demonstrated state without clearing a misconception or crossing a threshold.

chapters.caption: 01  Open Graph Memory: the course keeps a learner-specific, versioned snapshot.
02  Two earlier demo probes support this misconception; one new answer is not clearance.
03  Answer a fresh diagnostic and explain the fixed-voltage condition.
04  Pending evidence does not replace the last committed memory snapshot.
05  After demo processing commits, state improves without declaring mastery or crossing.
06  Inspect the next probe and open the evidence behind the updated memory.
07  The profile recommends another independent probe, not an automatic mastery claim.

verification.evidenceQuote: I = V/R. At fixed voltage, doubling resistance halves the current.
verification.provenance: Synthetic before/pending/after API fixtures exercise the real Graph Memory UI; no live worker, model or state reducer was run.

tutorials.name: shiksha-student-teacher-tutorial
tutorials.title: Learning and teaching, side by side
tutorials.note: Two actual application sessions are captured together. The teacher explicitly asks Insights for an update; its scripted reply uses the learner's real intercepted demo question and submitted check. This demonstrates a shared local fixture, not a live cloud telemetry feed or an automatic mastery decision.

chapters.caption: 01  Two separate accounts: the learner opens a course while the teacher views the class.
02  The learner asks a question; the teacher opens Insights and scopes it to that learner.
03  While the course answer arrives, the teacher asks about the learner's current activity.
04  The learner opens the check, chooses an answer and explains the reasoning.
05  The teacher asks what changed; the response uses the submitted demo attempt.
06  Both views remain visible: learner feedback and a scoped teaching next step.

tutorials.name: shiksha-challenges-tutorial
tutorials.title: Work through a guided challenge
tutorials.note: A guided challenge is generated and explored through the actual challenge UI. Task content, hints and solution are synthetic. Hints and a revealed solution are learning aids, not assessment proof.

chapters.caption: 01  Ask for a challenge that tests reasoning, not just recall.
02  Open the challenge and predict before viewing any help.
03  Choose Solution, then reveal just the first hint.
04  Reveal the last hint and compare the ratios yourself.
05  Reveal the worked solution: both currents are 4 mA.
06  Put the solution away and explain the reasoning in chat.

tutorials.name: shiksha-chat-tutorial

chapters.caption: 01  Open a course from the Teaching Assistant library, then choose Start Chat.

06  Review the result and tutor feedback. One answer is not proof of mastery.

tutorials.name: shiksha-circuit-tutorial
tutorials.title: Experiment in the Circuit Lab
tutorials.note: Hypothetical low-voltage circuit practice in the actual Circuit Lab. Numeric results are local fixtures, not live ngspice output or physical wiring instructions.

chapters.caption: 1. Request a hypothetical 6 V circuit; no physical wiring.
2. Open Circuit Lab. These readings are mocked locally.
3. Inspect the 6 V supply and the 1,000 ohm resistor.
4. Mock baseline: 6 V / 1,000 ohms = 6 mA.
5. Double R1 to 2,000 ohms, then run the local mock again.
6. Mock result: 6 V / 2,000 ohms = 3 mA, half the current.

tutorials.name: shiksha-companion-review-tutorial
tutorials.title: Review and undo Course Companion edits
tutorials.note: Chat only, Allow editing and Undo are exercised in the real builder. No course is created and no remote agent is changed.

chapters.caption: 01  Start a course draft with your own title, code and description.
02  Choose Chat only when you want advice without changing the form.
03  Enable editing, then explicitly ask the Companion to apply the proposal.
04  Inspect the highlighted changes before deciding whether to keep them.
05  Undo restores your original values. No Create submission is made.
